newsitem.title: ROMANIA: SOCCER-STEAUA SAVES ROMANIAN SOCCER FROM DISASTER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STEAUA SAVES ROMANIAN SOCCER FROM DISASTER.

text.p: Steaua Bucharest have salvaged some honour from a Romanian soccer system riven by scandal and a chronic cash shortage by clearing the first hurdle of the European Cup.

The 1986 winners looked authoritative in defeating Bulgarian champions CSKA Sofia 2-0 on Wednesday to qualify for the European Cup second preliminary round against Paris Saint Germain 5-3 on aggregate.
But two other Romanian clubs were unceremoniously eliminated from the UEFA Cup by rank outsiders and now return to the mediocrity and problems of the national championship.
KR Reykjavik beat Dinamo Bucharest, both home and away, while Otelul Galati were edged out by HIT Gorica, European competition newcomers from Slovenia.

Steaua, Romanian champions for the last five years, carry their share of the financial burden in the Romanian game but seem to be the only club blessed with adequate organisation and a proper training system.
Many sides have become bogged down in what newspapers have described as a "black market of points" negotiated between club presidents, trainers or players.

National team coach Anghel Iordanescu quit for a time last year to denounce what he said were "strategic games" organised by first division team officials. Club presidents, he said, were interested solely in acquiring villas and luxury cars.

The Romanian Soccer Federation has not escaped allegations of corruption either. Most charges against the governing body revolve around a long-running scandal that it skimmed off 10 percent on transfer fees involving players moving to foreign clubs.
Steaua are now demanding the return of about $1 million taken over the past five years. But Federation officials say they have plouged the money back into soccer.
Romania's new Sports Minister Sorin Stanescu has begun an investigation into the allegations but the Federation has resisted all attempts to examine its finances.
